segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle:
Shall in every case yield
the right-of-way
to moving traffic and pedestrians.

elements.justification: "a vehicle": the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed whole through ru.aggregate; "The driver" is a relational role, read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading), never an aggregate.

To yield the right-of-way is to grant precedence (DEF-NRS-484A-210: "unless one grants precedence to the other"): ego does not continue its movement while a party it must yield to is in conflict with it. The movement the section governs is backing (reading on this span): drv.motion.backing, 'it moves in the direction opposite to the one its body points', which is not a stand-in for the selected gear. "in every case": every backing movement, with no exception.

"traffic": the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway'); "moving": not at rest (drv.motion.at_rest does not hold), the contract's speed above the rest tolerance. "pedestrians": the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian, every pedestrian whether moving or not: pedestrians are already traffic, so "moving" qualifies traffic, else the words would name pedestrians in vain. Each is a road user other than ego, quantified in the rule.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: DEF-NRS-484A-210 "approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other"
operationalizations.convention: Traffic-conflict technique: two road users are in conflict where, projected at their current velocities, their centres approach within the time-to-collision horizon and their closest-approach centre distance is below the clearance at which their bodies would touch. Direction, speed and proximity, the factors the definition names, enter by degree through the projected velocities and positions.

applicability: Ego is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; driven: agency reading) and is backing at the observation (drv.motion.backing, p.rest_speed_tolerance), the movement the section governs (reading on s2).
obligation: At that observation no road user u other than ego that is a member of traffic (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic) not at rest (drv.motion.at_rest, p.rest_speed_tolerance), or a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) at rest or not, is in conflict with ego: not both prim.closest_approach_within(ego, u) with horizon p.conflict_horizon and prim.closest_approach_distance(ego, u) with the same horizon below p.conflict_clearance. Ego yields by not backing while such a conflict holds.

narrowings.why: 'The driver' is read through ego's controlled motion: a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven.

The line is subsection (3) of NRS 484B.113, 'Limitations on backing', whose items govern the backing of a vehicle: the yield is read on ego's backing movement. Read without that movement the words would bind every vehicle to yield to every moving road user at every moment, two vehicles each yielding to the other; the reading keeps every case of backing ('in every case').

scenarios.narrative: Ego backs out of a parking space while a motor vehicle t drives along the aisle behind it; projected at constant velocities their centres approach within p.conflict_horizon to a distance below p.conflict_clearance while ego keeps backing.

scenarios.narrative: Ego backs out of a parking space with no other road user in the scene.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: Ego drives forward along the aisle; it is not backing.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Scene of forbid, but the source declares kin.velocity absent: whether ego is backing cannot be read.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Ego backs toward a pedestrian standing still on its path; projected at ego's velocity the closest approach falls within the horizon below the clearance.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: Ego backs past a parked vehicle at rest whose body lies close to ego's path; no moving traffic and no pedestrian is present.

param_proposals.name: p.rest_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Stop-detection noise floor: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement, set at the resolution of the speed measurement so that a complete cessation from movement is recognized despite sensor jitter.
param_proposals.source: Naturalistic-driving and simulator stop-detection practice (SHRP 2 event coding; CARLA ground-truth velocity resolution).

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: Time-to-collision horizon of the traffic-conflict technique: a projected approach of the centres within this time counts toward the danger of a crash.
param_proposals.source: Hayward (1972) time-to-collision; Hyden (1987) Swedish Traffic Conflict Technique; van der Horst (1990) TTC thresholds.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_clearance
param_proposals.convention: Centre-to-centre distance at the projected closest approach below which the bodies of two passenger vehicles would touch or nearly touch (about a half-length plus a half-width of a design passenger car).
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book, design vehicle P dimensions.

segmentation.text: Every vehicle
driven upon a divided highway
must be driven only upon the right-hand roadway
and
must not be driven over, across or within any dividing space, barrier or section
or make any left turn, semicircular turn or U-turn,
except through an opening in the barrier or dividing section or space
or at a crossover or intersection established by a public authority.

elements.justification: "Every vehicle": the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed whole through ru.aggregate.

"divided highway" (DEF-NRS-484A-070: "a highway divided into two or more roadways by means of a physical barrier or dividing section"): a highway h (st.highway) on which (st.on_way) a median or divider lies (st.median_or_divider, 'physical barrier or dividing section between roadways'). "upon": ego's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a roadway lying on h (st.roadway) or a median or divider of h; st.highway is read only as the way the regions lie on. "driven": controlled motion (agency reading).

"dividing space, barrier or section": st.median_or_divider, 'physical barrier or dividing section between roadways', a space between roadways included. "over, across or within": ego's footprint overlaps the region (rel.occupies), which is each of the three; not a distance to it.

"through an opening in the barrier or dividing section or space": ego's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a median or divider of h whose opening attribute is set (st.median_or_divider: 'opening attribute where a crossover exists').

"a crossover": a median or divider of h with the opening attribute ('opening attribute where a crossover exists'); "intersection": ego's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) an st.intersection lying on h. "established by a public authority": status read through the feature's presence.

applicability: Ego is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; driven: agency reading) whose footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a roadway (st.roadway) or a median or divider (st.median_or_divider) lying on a highway h (st.on_way, st.highway) on which at least one median or divider lies.
obligation: At that observation ego's footprint overlaps no median or divider m lying on h, except a median or divider whose opening attribute is set; and no such overlap is judged at an observation at which ego's footprint also overlaps an intersection lying on h (st.intersection, st.on_way).

narrowings.why: 'driven' is read through ego's controlled motion: a vehicle on the road is taken to be driven.
'established by a public authority' is read through the presence of the crossover or intersection on the road.

segmentation.text: Every vehicle
driven upon a divided highway
must be driven only upon the right-hand roadway
and
must not be driven over, across or within any dividing space, barrier or section
or make any left turn, semicircular turn or U-turn,
except through an opening in the barrier or dividing section or space
or at a crossover or intersection established by a public authority.

elements.justification: "Every vehicle": the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed whole through ru.aggregate.

"divided highway" (DEF-NRS-484A-070: "a highway divided into two or more roadways by means of a physical barrier or dividing section"): a highway h (st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines') on which (st.on_way, 'the public way ... a structure region lies on') a median or divider lies (st.median_or_divider, 'physical barrier or dividing section between roadways'). "upon": ego's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a roadway lying on h (st.roadway: 'separate roadways of a divided highway are separate') or a median or divider of h; st.highway is read only as the way the regions lie on, never as the roadway. "driven": controlled motion (agency reading).

"the right-hand roadway": of the roadways of h, the one lying to the right of the dividing section as ego travels, so every median or divider of h lies to ego's left: prim.region_lateral_offset(ego, m) positive ('the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user'). "only upon": at every observation at which ego occupies a roadway of h (rel.occupies, st.roadway).

"through an opening in the barrier or dividing section or space": ego's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a median or divider of h whose opening attribute is set (st.median_or_divider: 'opening attribute where a crossover exists'). The exception closes the sentence and covers each duty it lists: passing through an opening necessarily leaves the right-hand roadway.

"a crossover": a median or divider of h with the opening attribute ('opening attribute where a crossover exists'); "intersection": ego's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) an st.intersection lying on h ('an intersection lies on every way that meets there'). "established by a public authority": the legal status of a feature, read through its presence (status reading).

applicability: Ego is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; driven: agency reading) whose footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a roadway r (st.roadway) lying on a highway h (st.on_way, st.highway) on which at least one median or divider lies (st.median_or_divider, st.on_way).
obligation: At that observation every median or divider m lying on h lies to ego's left: prim.region_lateral_offset(ego, m) is positive. Not judged at an observation at which ego's footprint overlaps a median or divider of h with the opening attribute, or an intersection lying on h (st.intersection, st.on_way).

narrowings.why: 'driven' is read through ego's controlled motion: a vehicle on the road is taken to be driven.
'established by a public authority' is read through the presence of the crossover or intersection on the road.

segmentation.text: A driver of a motor vehicle
shall: Exercise due care
to avoid a collision with a pedestrian.

elements.justification: 'motor vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle, the definition that applies: 'every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails', which 'does not include an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'; the run's reading classifies the classes under that id, so the aggregate is claimed whole and never expanded into class atoms. 'A driver of' names who controls the vehicle, no class: it is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (narrowing, observable_reading agency).

'a collision' is rel.contact: 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)'. Its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: a near miss' does not apply: the collision itself is what the duty is to avoid, and the approach short of contact is read by the operationalization of 'due care', not by this atom. 'a pedestrian' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian: 'a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'; claimed whole and read for every road user of the scene other than ego.

operationalizations.convention: Traffic-conflict technique: while the motor vehicle moves (drv.motion.at_rest under p.rest_speed_tolerance does not hold), a pedestrian whose centre it approaches within the time-to-collision horizon p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below p.pedestrian_conflict_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance) is a conflict the driver's care did not avoid; the projected distance enters the bound itself, so a nearer approach is a graver one. Care is a state of mind and the standard is the whole duty: the rule is a surrogate.

applicability: ego is a motor vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle). The duty is judged at every observation.
obligation: At every observation, for every road user p of the scene other than ego that is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian): either ego is at rest (drv.motion.at_rest with p.rest_speed_tolerance), or ego and p are not in contact (rel.contact) and it is not the case that their centres approach within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) with a centre distance at that closest approach below p.pedestrian_conflict_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance). With no pedestrian in the scene the duty is met.

narrowings.why: 'A driver' is read through the motor vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.

'due care' is read only as the avoidance of contact and of a projected close approach to a pedestrian while the vehicle moves; lookout, warning and attention are read only through that outcome, and contact made while the vehicle is at rest is not read as a want of care.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: ego, a passenger car (ru.motor_vehicle), drives along a roadway toward a pedestrian crossing in front of it; the centres are projected to approach within the horizon to a distance below the pedestrian clearance, and ego keeps moving.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: ego drives along an empty road with no pedestrian anywhere in the scene: the duty binds ego alone and is met.

segmentation.text: It is unlawful for any person to drive or operate
a vehicle of any kind or character
at: A rate of speed
greater than is reasonable or proper, having due regard for the traffic, surface and width of the highway, the weather and other highway conditions.

elements.justification: 'to drive or operate' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency): its speed (kin.speed, 'magnitude of velocity'), whoever or whatever controls it.

'vehicle' admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle: 'every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', except 'Devices moved by human power or used exclusively upon stationary rails', 'Electric bicycles', electric personal assistive mobility devices and 'An electric scooter'; claimed whole. 'of any kind or character' adds no restriction.
'A rate of speed' is kin.speed, 'magnitude of velocity' in m/s; kin.accel_longitudinal's 'Not a stand-in for: speed' confirms speed is read directly.

operationalizations.standard: a rate of speed greater than is reasonable or proper, having due regard for the traffic, surface and width of the highway, the weather and other highway conditions
operationalizations.convention: Stopping-sight-distance model of highway design (AASHTO Green Book), with the curve side-friction and lane-width relations of the same guides. Surface and weather select the deceleration: p.stopping_decel_ice where env.ice_or_snow holds, else p.stopping_decel_wet where env.wet_road or env.precipitation holds, else p.stopping_decel_dry (Term.cond over drv.motion.stopping_distance calls with p.perception_reaction_time). The stopping distance may not exceed the sight distance of the place (st.sight_distance) nor the visibility distance (env.visibility); for every road user ahead of ego in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane), the traffic, the gap (rel.surface_gap) may not fall below the speed times p.perception_reaction_time; the speed squared times the curvature (st.curvature) may not exceed p.curve_lateral_accel; the speed times p.lane_width_speed_time may not exceed the width (st.lane_width) of the lane ego occupies (st.lane, rel.occupies). Each measured magnitude enters its bound. The standard is the whole duty: the rule is a surrogate.

applicability: ego is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle); the duty is judged at every observation.
obligation: At every observation, with D the stopping distance of ego (drv.motion.stopping_distance with p.perception_reaction_time and the deceleration selected by Term.cond: p.stopping_decel_ice where env.ice_or_snow holds, else p.stopping_decel_wet where env.wet_road or env.precipitation holds, else p.stopping_decel_dry): D is at or below st.sight_distance at ego's place and at or below env.visibility; ego's speed (kin.speed) squared times st.curvature at its place is at or below p.curve_lateral_accel; for every lane l ego occupies (rel.occupies), ego's speed times p.lane_width_speed_time is at or below st.lane_width of l; and for every road user u other than ego that is ahead of ego in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane), the gap between them (rel.surface_gap) is at or above ego's speed times p.perception_reaction_time. With no such road user the last clause is met.

narrowings.why: 'drive or operate' is read through the vehicle's motion, whoever or whatever controls it.

The factors are read only through the contracts named: traffic through the road users ahead in ego's lane (crossing and oncoming traffic, and its density, are not read); surface through wet and icy or snow-covered states; width through the width of the lane ego occupies; weather through precipitation and visibility distance; the catch-all 'other highway conditions' only through curvature and the sight distance of the place (grade, darkness and works are not read).
The place at which st.sight_distance and st.curvature are read is each lane ego occupies (st.lane, rel.occupies), the regions the width clause selects; no other region of ego's place is read.

scenarios.name: idle

scenarios.name: blind

scenarios.name: branch_2

param_proposals.name: p.perception_reaction_time
param_proposals.convention: Brake reaction time of the stopping-sight-distance model: the time from the appearance of a hazard to the application of the brakes.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book, stopping sight distance

param_proposals.name: p.stopping_decel_dry
param_proposals.convention: Deceleration a driver attains in a controlled stop on a dry paved surface.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book and braking studies (Fambro et al., NCHRP 400)

param_proposals.name: p.stopping_decel_wet

param_proposals.name: p.curve_lateral_accel
param_proposals.convention: Side-friction limit of horizontal curve design: the lateral acceleration a curve may impose on a vehicle at a comfortable, safe speed.

param_proposals.convention: Lane width per unit of speed from the lane-width and design-speed relation of highway design guides (a full-width lane for a high design speed): the speed times it may not exceed the lane's width.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book lane widths by design speed

segmentation.text: When a vehicle enters an intersection
controlled by a traffic-control signal which is installed and has its vehicular signals uncovered,
but is inoperative at the time the vehicle enters the intersection,
the driver of the vehicle
shall proceed as if a stop sign had been erected at each entrance to the intersection and shall stop
at a clearly marked stop line
or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection
or, if there is none, at the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.
After making such a stop,
the driver
shall proceed cautiously,
yielding to vehicles
which have previously completed a stop or are within the intersection.

elements.justification: "a vehicle": the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. "enters an intersection": the observation at which ego's footprint comes to overlap (rel.occupies) an intersection i (st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet'), having occupied at the observation before, and not overlapping i, a carrier c (a travel region of a kind st.lane_enters admits) whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters, 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'); never inferred from distance or heading.

"traffic-control signal" (DEF-NRS-484A-290 'any official traffic-control device ... by which traffic is alternately directed to stop or proceed'): a dev.traffic_signal head, 'a signal head', not a pedestrian head, which is no vehicular signal. "controlled by": the head governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection') the intersection i or ego's approach carrier c; dev.governs is not a position. "installed and has its vehicular signals uncovered": the head is present with its uncovered attribute ('uncovered attribute for an installed head whose faces are not covered'); its official status is read through its presence.

dev.inoperative: 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication', exactly the words. "at the time the vehicle enters": read at the entry observation. The signal is inoperative where every head governing c or i is inoperative there, and at least one such head exists.
"the vehicle": the same vehicle as a1 (admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle); "the driver" read through its controlled motion (agency reading).

"shall stop": a stop when required, DEF-NRS-484A-255 "complete cessation from movement" (DEF-NRS-484A-260 governs a stop 'when prohibited' and does not apply to a required stop): drv.motion.at_rest. "proceed as if a stop sign had been erected at each entrance": ego owes at its own entrance what a stop-sign approach owes, the halt this node judges at the place a6-a8 name and the yield its sibling NRS_484B_250_4_o2 judges; the signs at the other entrances bind the other vehicles, each judged as its own subject.

st.stop_line, 'the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device', tied to ego's approach carrier c by st.entrance_of ('the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks'), never by distance. "at" the line: ego's body within p.stop_point_tolerance of it (st.region_geometry distance) and not past it, the side read along c's designated direction (st.lane_direction, sign of prim.region_offset_along), as the ontology's approach convention states. "clearly marked": the represented line is read as the clearly marked one (status reading).

"if there is none": the source's list of stop lines marking c is complete and none marks it. "the crosswalk on the near side": the st.crosswalk marking c (st.entrance_of), the crossing ego reaches first. "before entering": ego halts short of it with its footprint not overlapping it (rel.occupies false), within p.stop_point_tolerance outside it (st.region_geometry), side read along c (st.lane_direction, prim.region_offset_along).

"if there is none": neither a stop line nor a crosswalk marks c (lists complete). "the point nearest the intersection": c's entrance end at i (st.lane_enters); the halt counts there where ego's footprint does not overlap i (rel.occupies false) and its body lies within p.stop_point_tolerance of i (st.region_geometry). "where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway": a perception, read through the place it secures (perception reading): the point nearest the intersection is its edge, from which the view of the crossing way is widest.

applicability: Ego is a vehicle (driven: agency reading) and the judged observation is an entry of ego into an intersection i: ego's footprint overlaps i (rel.occupies, st.intersection) and at the observation before it did not, and occupied a carrier c whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters); at that entry at least one traffic signal head (dev.traffic_signal) governs c or i (dev.governs) and every such head is inoperative (dev.inoperative).
obligation: Event and target: the entry of ego into i through c described in the applicability. Place: the stop line marking c (st.stop_line, st.entrance_of) where one is recorded; else, where the source's list for c is complete and no stop line marks it, the crosswalk marking c (st.crosswalk, st.entrance_of), a halt there being short of it with ego's footprint not overlapping it; else the entrance end of c at i, a halt there being outside i. A halt counts at the place where ego is at rest (drv.motion.at_rest, p.rest_speed_tolerance) on c with its body within p.stop_point_tolerance of the place (st.region_geometry) and not past it, the side read along c's designated direction (st.lane_direction, sign of prim.region_offset_along). Search: from the entry back to the approach start, the last observation before the entry at which ego, on a carrier the place marks, is outside the place's stopping zone upstream (off the place, short of it along c's direction and farther from it than p.stop_point_tolerance), or back to ego's previous entry into i, whichever comes first; nothing else ends it, not the start of the recording, not ego's first observation, not a distance travelled. Only an observed exit from the stopping zone upstream begins a new approach; crossing the place, a lateral move, a change of carrier within the same entry or a reverse within the zone does not, and none loses a halt already made. Verdict: compliant where the search finds such a halt; violated where it reaches the approach start or the previous entry without one; unknown where it reaches neither (the approach began before the recording), where whether the entry occurred is unknown (no observation of ego before it, ego on no mapped carrier, or c's association with the place unobserved), where which place governs turns on an unobserved association or an incomplete list, or where the signal's state at the entry is unobserved.

'where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway' is read through the place it secures: the point nearest the intersection, the entrance end of ego's approach carrier, outside the intersection.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
within an intersection
intending to turn to the left
shall yield
the right-of-way
to any vehicle approaching from the opposite direction
which is within the intersection
or so close thereto as to constitute an immediate hazard,
but such driver,
having so yielded
and having given a signal when and as required,
may make such left turn
and the drivers of all other vehicles approaching the intersection from the opposite direction
shall yield
the right-of-way
to the vehicle making the left turn.

elements.justification: "a vehicle": the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; "The driver" read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading).
"within an intersection": ego's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) an intersection i (st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet'); i is the region the intention f3 is declared at.

"yield": granting precedence (DEF-NRS-484A-210 "unless one grants precedence to the other"): ego does not proceed while the vehicle with the right-of-way is in conflict with it, so ego is at rest (drv.motion.at_rest) or not in conflict (operationalization of f5).

"any vehicle": every road user b other than ego of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. "approaching from the opposite direction": read, as rel.oncoming's contract directs, through the carriers: b's approach carrier (the carrier whose entrance end is i that b occupies, or the one from which it entered i; st.lane_enters, rel.occupies) and ego's (the carrier from which ego entered i) carry opposed designated directions (st.lane_direction), not through the current headings, which a turn changes.
"which is within the intersection": b's footprint overlaps the same i (rel.occupies).

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: DEF-NRS-484A-210 "approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other"
operationalizations.convention: Traffic-conflict technique: two road users are in conflict where, projected at their current velocities, their centres approach within the time-to-collision horizon and their closest-approach centre distance is below the clearance at which their bodies would touch. Direction, speed and proximity enter by degree through the projected velocities and positions.

operationalizations.standard: so close thereto as to constitute an immediate hazard
operationalizations.convention: Gap acceptance: an approaching vehicle is an immediate hazard where its time to reach the intersection is below the critical headway for a left turn, read as the ground distance from its body to the intersection (st.region_geometry) at or below its speed (kin.speed) times the critical headway; distance and speed enter by degree.

intentions.meaning: The road user's current plan includes turning left at the target region.

applicability: Ego is a vehicle (driven: agency reading) whose footprint overlaps an intersection i (rel.occupies, st.intersection) and which declares int.left_turn at i at the judged observation.
obligation: For every vehicle b other than ego whose approach to i is opposite to ego's (b's approach carrier, the carrier entering i that b occupies or the one from which it entered i, and the carrier from which ego entered i carry directions whose dot product is below minus p.opposite_direction_tolerance; st.lane_direction, st.lane_enters) and that either overlaps i or occupies its approach carrier with the ground distance from its body to i (st.region_geometry) at or below its speed (kin.speed) times p.immediate_hazard_time: ego is at rest (drv.motion.at_rest, p.rest_speed_tolerance) or not in conflict with b, that is not both prim.closest_approach_within(ego, b) with horizon p.conflict_horizon and prim.closest_approach_distance(ego, b) with the same horizon below p.conflict_clearance.

segmentation.text: Every vehicle
driven upon a divided highway
must be driven only upon the right-hand roadway
and
must not be driven over, across or within any dividing space, barrier or section
or make any left turn, semicircular turn or U-turn,
except through an opening in the barrier or dividing section or space
or at a crossover or intersection established by a public authority.

elements.justification: "Every vehicle": the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed whole through ru.aggregate.

"divided highway" (DEF-NRS-484A-070: "a highway divided into two or more roadways by means of a physical barrier or dividing section"): a highway h (st.highway) on which (st.on_way) a median or divider lies (st.median_or_divider). "upon": ego's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a roadway lying on h (st.roadway) or a median or divider of h. "driven": controlled motion (agency reading).

"left turn": drv.motion.left_turn, a leftward heading change within the turn band over the window, not the turn indicator and not a declared intention. "U-turn": drv.motion.u_turn, whose contract quotes DEF-NRS-484B-077 "the turning of a vehicle upon a highway so as to proceed in the opposite direction, whether accomplished by one continuous movement or not". "semicircular turn": a turn through a half circle reverses the direction of travel, the observable the U-turn concept recognizes, so it is read by drv.motion.u_turn. Alternative acts sharing one occasion.

"through an opening": ego's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a median or divider of h whose opening attribute is set ('opening attribute where a crossover exists') at some moment of the turn: a turn made through an opening passes through it, it is not inside it throughout.

"a crossover": a median or divider of h with the opening attribute; "intersection": ego's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) an st.intersection lying on h at some moment of the turn. "established by a public authority": status read through the feature's presence.

applicability: Ego is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; driven: agency reading); at the judged observation ego's left turn (drv.motion.left_turn with p.turn_window, p.left_turn_min_angle, p.left_turn_max_angle) or U-turn (drv.motion.u_turn with p.turn_window, p.u_turn_min_angle, p.u_turn_max_angle) is recognized (the concept rises), and at some observation while it was under way ego's footprint overlapped (rel.occupies) a roadway (st.roadway) or a median or divider lying on a highway h on which a median or divider lies (st.on_way, st.highway, st.median_or_divider).
obligation: Violated at that recognition unless, at some observation while the turn was under way, ego's footprint overlapped a median or divider of h with the opening attribute set, or an intersection lying on h (st.intersection, st.on_way); compliant where it did.

narrowings.why: 'driven' is read through ego's controlled motion: a vehicle on the road is taken to be driven.
'established by a public authority' is read through the presence of the crossover or intersection on the road.

param_proposals.source: Vehicle-dynamics practice for turn-onset detection from yaw-rate sensors.

segmentation.text: When a vehicle enters an intersection
controlled by a traffic-control signal which is installed and has its vehicular signals uncovered,
but is inoperative at the time the vehicle enters the intersection,
the driver of the vehicle
shall proceed as if a stop sign had been erected at each entrance to the intersection and shall stop
at a clearly marked stop line
or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection
or, if there is none, at the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.
After making such a stop,
the driver
shall proceed cautiously,
yielding to vehicles
which have previously completed a stop or are within the intersection.

elements.justification: "a vehicle": the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. "enters an intersection": the observation at which ego's footprint comes to overlap (rel.occupies) an intersection i (st.intersection), having occupied at the observation before a carrier c whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters); read through a past operator, since the judged observations follow it.
"traffic-control signal": a dev.traffic_signal head ('a signal head') governing (dev.governs) i or c; installed and uncovered: present with its uncovered attribute. Not a pedestrian head.

dev.inoperative: 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication', read at the observation of ego's entry into i ("at the time the vehicle enters"), through a past operator: every head governing c or i inoperative there, at least one.
"the vehicle": ego (admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle); "the driver" read through its controlled motion (agency reading).

"such a stop" is the stop a5-a8 require, carried in full: ego at rest (drv.motion.at_rest, "complete cessation from movement") on its approach carrier c at the governing place, the stop line marking c (st.stop_line, st.entrance_of), else short of the crosswalk marking c with its footprint not overlapping it (st.crosswalk, rel.occupies), else outside i at c's entrance end, body within p.stop_point_tolerance of the place (st.region_geometry), side read along c (st.lane_direction, prim.region_offset_along), found between the approach start and ego's entry into i as NRS_484B_250_4_o1 states. A halt elsewhere is not such a stop. "After": the judged observations follow that halt.
"the driver": of ego, a vehicle (admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), read through its controlled motion (agency reading).

"yielding": granting precedence: ego does not proceed while a vehicle it yields to is in conflict with it, so at every judged observation ego is at rest (drv.motion.at_rest) or not in conflict with that vehicle (operationalization of a11). "vehicles": road users of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle other than ego.

"are within the intersection": b's footprint overlaps i (rel.occupies, st.intersection). "have previously completed a stop": b, on a carrier c_b other than c whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters), came to rest there (drv.motion.at_rest) and the rest it came to began before ego's halt on c began, and b still occupies c_b; once b enters i it is within the intersection.

operationalizations.convention: Traffic-conflict technique: ego proceeds cautiously toward a vehicle it yields to where, projected at their current velocities, their centres do not approach within the time-to-collision horizon to a distance below the clearance at which their bodies would touch; the positions and velocities enter by degree.

applicability: Ego is a vehicle (driven: agency reading) that entered an intersection i from a carrier c (st.lane_enters) at an observation at which at least one traffic signal head governed c or i (dev.traffic_signal, dev.governs) and every such head was inoperative (dev.inoperative), and that made, between the approach start and that entry, the stop a9 describes at the governing place on c (drv.motion.at_rest, p.rest_speed_tolerance, p.stop_point_tolerance); judged at every observation from that entry while ego's footprint overlaps i (rel.occupies). Where the history the stop's search needs precedes the recording, the applicability is unknown.
obligation: For every vehicle b other than ego that overlaps i, or that occupies a carrier c_b other than c whose entrance end is i and came to rest there (drv.motion.at_rest) at an onset of rest earlier than the onset of ego's halt on c: ego is at rest (drv.motion.at_rest) or not in conflict with b, that is not both prim.closest_approach_within(ego, b) with horizon p.conflict_horizon and prim.closest_approach_distance(ego, b) with the same horizon below p.conflict_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'the driver' is read through ego's controlled motion.

'cautiously' is read through the conflict with the vehicles ego yields to: ego proceeds without a projected closest approach to such a vehicle below the clearance within the horizon; caution toward other road users is not read by this rule.
A vehicle with precedence that keeps waiting at its own entrance is not in conflict with ego; ego proceeding while it waits is not read as a failure to yield.

segmentation.text: Except when traffic is being controlled by a police officer or a traffic-control signal:
When proper signs have been erected,
the driver of a vehicle
shall stop or yield
at a clearly marked stop line
or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection
or, if there is none, then at the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.
After having stopped or, in the event of a yield sign, slowed or stopped,
the driver
shall yield
the right-of-way
to other vehicles which have entered the intersection from such through highway
or which are approaching so closely on such through highway as to constitute an immediate hazard
during the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection.

elements.justification: "traffic": the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, of which ego, a vehicle using the highway, is a member. "being controlled by a police officer": a dev.human_direction of role police_officer ('a person directing traffic and the direction given'; DEF-NRS-484A-180 'every officer authorized to direct or regulate traffic') governing (dev.governs) ego's approach carrier c or the intersection i at ego's entry. "or a traffic-control signal": a dev.traffic_signal head governing c or i that is not inoperative (dev.inoperative, 'showing no valid indication', does not hold) at the entry: a dark head controls no traffic.

"proper signs": a stop sign (dev.stop_sign, 'regulatory sign requiring a full halt') or a yield sign (dev.yield_sign, 'regulatory sign requiring yielding without a mandatory halt') governing (dev.governs) ego's approach carrier c, whose entrance end is the intersection i (st.lane_enters); "proper" and "erected" are the signs' legal status, read through their presence (status reading). A sign is not a signal.
"a vehicle": the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; "the driver" read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading).

"stop": a stop when required, DEF-NRS-484A-255 "complete cessation from movement" (DEF-NRS-484A-260 governs a stop 'when prohibited'): drv.motion.at_rest, owed under a stop sign. "yield" at the place, under a yield sign alone: the line's own later words state what it is, "in the event of a yield sign, slowed or stopped": at rest at the place, or slowed, read as ego decelerating (drv.motion.decelerating, its acceleration along its heading below the negative tolerance) at some observation within the distance window p.yield_slowing_distance travelled before it is within the place's stopping zone, a .path window that reads kin.path_length.

st.stop_line, 'the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device', tied to ego's approach carrier c by st.entrance_of, never by distance. "at" the line: ego's body within p.stop_point_tolerance of it (st.region_geometry) and not past it, side read along c's designated direction (st.lane_direction, prim.region_offset_along). "clearly marked": the represented line is read as the clearly marked one (status reading).

"if there is none": the source's list of stop lines marking c is complete and none marks it. "the crosswalk on the near side": the st.crosswalk marking c (st.entrance_of). "before entering": ego halts short of it with its footprint not overlapping it (rel.occupies false), within p.stop_point_tolerance outside it (st.region_geometry), side read along c (st.lane_direction, prim.region_offset_along).

"if there is none": neither a stop line nor a crosswalk marks c (lists complete). "then at the point nearest the intersection": c's entrance end at i (st.lane_enters); the act counts there where ego's footprint does not overlap i (rel.occupies false) and its body lies within p.stop_point_tolerance of i (st.region_geometry). "where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway": a perception, read through the place it secures (perception reading).

applicability: Ego is a vehicle (driven: agency reading) and the judged observation is an entry of ego into an intersection i (its footprint overlaps i and did not at the observation before, when it occupied a carrier c whose entrance end is i; st.lane_enters) where a stop sign or a yield sign governs c (dev.stop_sign, dev.yield_sign, dev.governs); not where, at that entry, a police officer directs (dev.human_direction role police_officer governing c or i) or a traffic signal head governing c or i is not inoperative (dev.traffic_signal, dev.inoperative).
obligation: Event and target: the entry of ego into i through c. Place: the stop line marking c (st.stop_line, st.entrance_of) where one is recorded; else, where the source's list for c is complete and no stop line marks it, the crosswalk marking c, the act there being short of it with ego's footprint not overlapping it; else the entrance end of c at i, outside i. Act: where a stop sign governs c, a halt, ego at rest (drv.motion.at_rest, p.rest_speed_tolerance) on c with its body within p.stop_point_tolerance of the place (st.region_geometry) and not past it, side read along c's designated direction (st.lane_direction, sign of prim.region_offset_along); where only a yield sign governs c, that halt, or an observation at which ego, on c, is within the place's stopping zone and not past the place and had decelerated (drv.motion.decelerating, p.decel_tolerance, p.rest_speed_tolerance) at some observation of the .path window of length p.yield_slowing_distance behind it. Search: from the entry back to the approach start, the last observation before the entry at which ego, on a carrier the place marks, is outside the place's stopping zone upstream (off the place, short of it along c's direction and farther from it than p.stop_point_tolerance), or back to ego's previous entry into i, whichever comes first; nothing else ends it, not the start of the recording, not ego's first observation, not a distance travelled. Only an observed exit from the stopping zone upstream begins a new approach; crossing the place, a lateral move, a change of carrier within the same entry or a reverse within the zone does not, and none loses an act already done. Verdict: compliant where the search finds the act; violated where it reaches the approach start or the previous entry without it; unknown where it reaches neither (the approach began before the recording), where whether the entry occurred is unknown, where which place governs turns on an unobserved association or an incomplete list, or where the sign's governance of c is unobserved.

narrowings.why: 'the driver' is read through ego's controlled motion.
'proper' and 'erected' are read through the presence of the stop or yield sign governing ego's approach.
'clearly marked' is read through the presence of the represented stop line; the paint's clarity is not modelled.
'where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway' is read through the place it secures: the entrance end of ego's approach carrier, outside the intersection.

'yield' at the place under a yield sign is read as the line's own words state it, 'slowed or stopped'; 'slowed' is read as a deceleration within a distance window before the stopping zone, not as a reduction to any particular speed.

segmentation.text: Except when traffic is being controlled by a police officer or a traffic-control signal:
When proper signs have been erected,
the driver of a vehicle
shall stop or yield
at a clearly marked stop line
or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection
or, if there is none, then at the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.
After having stopped or, in the event of a yield sign, slowed or stopped,
the driver
shall yield
the right-of-way
to other vehicles which have entered the intersection from such through highway
or which are approaching so closely on such through highway as to constitute an immediate hazard
during the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection.

elements.justification: "traffic": the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, of which ego is a member. "being controlled by a police officer": a dev.human_direction of role police_officer governing (dev.governs) ego's approach carrier c or the intersection i at ego's entry. "or a traffic-control signal": a dev.traffic_signal head governing c or i that is not inoperative (dev.inoperative) at the entry.
"proper signs": a stop sign (dev.stop_sign) or a yield sign (dev.yield_sign) governing (dev.governs) ego's approach carrier c, whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters); status read through presence.
"a vehicle": the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; "the driver" read through its controlled motion (agency reading).

The referent is the act g4-g7 require on ego's approach c to i, carried in full: under a stop sign (dev.stop_sign), "having stopped" at the governing place (the stop line marking c, st.stop_line and st.entrance_of; else short of the crosswalk marking c, st.crosswalk and rel.occupies false; else outside i at c's entrance end), ego at rest (drv.motion.at_rest, DEF-NRS-484A-255 "complete cessation from movement") with its body within p.stop_point_tolerance of the place (st.region_geometry), side read along c (st.lane_direction, prim.region_offset_along); "in the event of a yield sign" (dev.yield_sign), "slowed or stopped": that halt, or ego within the place's stopping zone having decelerated (drv.motion.decelerating) within the .path window p.yield_slowing_distance behind (kin.path_length); found between the approach start and ego's entry into i, as NRS_484B_257_1_o1 states. "After": the judged observations follow that act.
"the driver": of ego, a vehicle (admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), read through its controlled motion (agency reading).

"shall yield": granting precedence (DEF-NRS-484A-210 "unless one grants precedence to the other"): ego is at rest (drv.motion.at_rest) or not in conflict with the vehicle it yields to (operationalization of g11).

"other vehicles": road users b other than ego of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. "have entered the intersection": b's footprint overlaps i (rel.occupies) after an entry from a carrier c_b whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters), read through a past operator. "such through highway" (DEF-NRS-484A-275: "on which vehicular traffic is given the right-of-way, and at the entrances to which vehicular traffic from intersecting highways is required by law to yield"): c_b lies (st.on_way) on a highway (st.highway) on which ego's carrier c does not lie, and no stop sign or yield sign governs c_b (dev.stop_sign, dev.yield_sign, dev.governs): traffic on it is given the right-of-way while ego's entrance yields.

"during the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection": ego's footprint overlaps i (rel.occupies) and ego is not at rest (drv.motion.at_rest does not hold); the duty is judged at those observations.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: DEF-NRS-484A-210 "approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other"
operationalizations.convention: Traffic-conflict technique: two road users are in conflict where, projected at their current velocities, their centres approach within the time-to-collision horizon and their closest-approach centre distance is below the clearance at which their bodies would touch. Direction, speed and proximity enter by degree through the projected velocities and positions.

operationalizations.standard: approaching so closely on such through highway as to constitute an immediate hazard
operationalizations.convention: Gap acceptance: a vehicle b on a carrier c_b of the through highway whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters, st.on_way, rel.occupies) is an immediate hazard during ego's crossing where its time to reach the intersection is below the critical headway, read as the ground distance from its body to i (st.region_geometry) at or below its speed (kin.speed) times the critical headway; distance and speed enter by degree.

applicability: Ego is a vehicle (driven: agency reading) that entered an intersection i from a carrier c (st.lane_enters) governed by a stop sign or a yield sign (dev.stop_sign, dev.yield_sign, dev.governs), where at that entry no police officer directed (dev.human_direction role police_officer governing c or i) and no traffic signal head governing c or i was operating (dev.traffic_signal, dev.inoperative); and that made on c, between the approach start and that entry, the act g8 names (under a stop sign a halt at the governing place; under a yield sign alone that halt or a deceleration within p.yield_slowing_distance before the place's stopping zone; drv.motion.at_rest, drv.motion.decelerating, p.rest_speed_tolerance, p.decel_tolerance, p.stop_point_tolerance). Judged at every observation from that entry at which ego overlaps i and is not at rest. Where the history that act's search needs precedes the recording, the applicability is unknown.
obligation: For every vehicle b other than ego that either overlaps i after an entry from a carrier c_b of the through highway (c_b lies on a highway on which c does not lie, and no stop sign or yield sign governs c_b), or occupies such a carrier c_b whose entrance end is i with the ground distance from its body to i (st.region_geometry) at or below its speed (kin.speed) times p.immediate_hazard_time: ego is not in conflict with b, that is not both prim.closest_approach_within(ego, b) with horizon p.conflict_horizon and prim.closest_approach_distance(ego, b) with the same horizon below p.conflict_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'the driver' is read through ego's controlled motion.
'proper' and 'erected' are read through the presence of the stop or yield sign governing ego's approach.

segmentation.text: A signal of intention to turn right or left, or otherwise turn a vehicle from a direct course, shall be given continuously during
not less than the last 100 feet traveled
in a business or residential district
and not less than the last 300 feet traveled
in any other area
prior to changing the course of a vehicle.
This rule shall be observed, regardless of the weather.

elements.justification: A signal 'of intention' is the signal itself: sig.turn_indicator, 'the turn indicator state ∈ {off, left, right}', or sig.hand_signal, 'a driver's or rider's arm signal; meaning ∈ {no_signal, left, right, stop_or_slow, re_enter}', on the side of the turn ('to turn right or left, or otherwise turn ... from a direct course'), the turn itself being read by t8's concepts. 'given continuously during' is that matching signal at every observation of the window (holdsFor): an observation with the indicator off and no matching arm signal breaks it. 'Not a stand-in for: the turn or lane change itself' is respected: the signal is judged separately from the turn. 'a vehicle' is DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', except 'Devices moved by human power', 'Electric bicycles', electric personal assistive mobility devices and 'An electric scooter'), claimed whole.

'the last 100 feet traveled' is a window measured in the distance ego travelled behind the onset (a .path window), read through kin.path_length, 'distance travelled along the body's path since the start of the trace, monotone'; the figure is the law's literal. It selects the window where t5 holds.
'the last 300 feet traveled' is the same .path window with the law's other literal, through kin.path_length; it selects the window where t7 holds.

'changing the course of a vehicle' is a change of its heading to one side from an observed onset: drv.motion.left_turn_from_onset or drv.motion.right_turn_from_onset, each recognizing a continuous turning stretch whose heading change reaches the turn angle. 'prior to' places the window before the observed onset: the observation at which drv.motion.turning_left (or drv.motion.turning_right) last became true before the recognition, as those concepts' act records declare it. 'a vehicle' is DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed whole.

assumptions.meaning: The map or the trace declares the territory at the road user's position a business district or a residence district.
The map or the trace declares the territory at the road user's position a business district or a residence district.

residues.why: The duty holds in every weather: no condition of the weather restricts it, so the duty is the same whether or not its words hold.

applicability: ego is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle). The judged observation is the recognition of a left turn from an observed onset (drv.motion.left_turn_from_onset with p.left_turn_min_angle, p.turn_yaw_tolerance, p.rest_speed_tolerance, p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph) or of a right turn from an observed onset (drv.motion.right_turn_from_onset with p.right_turn_min_angle and the same tolerances).
obligation: Event, recognition and history (rule 4d): the event is the change of course; it is recognized at the judged observation; its observed onset is the last observation at which drv.motion.turning_left (for a left turn; drv.motion.turning_right for a right turn, each with p.turn_yaw_tolerance and p.rest_speed_tolerance) became true, the turning state having held at every observation since (a since operator: turning since (rise of turning and W)). W, read at that onset: where asm.business_or_residence_district holds there, at every observation of the window of the literal 100 ft of path travelled by ego behind the onset (holdsFor .path, kin.path_length), ego's turn indicator is left (sig.turn_indicator = left) or its arm signal means left (sig.hand_signal = left); where it does not hold, the same over the window of the literal 300 ft. For a right turn the matching side is right. The window ends at the onset and is the words' own bound; a window that reaches past the start of the recording is unknown (windowTruncated), as is the duty where the assumption is undeclared and the two windows decide differently. Conduct after the onset is not read.

narrowings.why: A change of course is read as a turn whose heading change from its observed onset reaches the turn angle; a lane change or a gentle departure from the course, whose heading change stays below it, is not read, and a road bend followed through that angle in one turning stretch is read as a turn.

segmentation.text: Whenever any vehicle is stopped
at a marked crosswalk or at any unmarked crosswalk at an intersection
to permit a pedestrian to cross the roadway
the driver of any other vehicle approaching from the rear
shall not overtake and pass such stopped vehicle.

elements.justification: "any vehicle": the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed whole through ru.aggregate ('membership of a legal aggregate'), never expanded into classes; it is a road user b other than ego ("any other vehicle" in s4), quantified in the rule, not a binder. "is stopped": drv.motion.at_rest, whose contract carries "complete cessation from movement" as a speed at or below the rest tolerance; it is b's state of motion, not its brake lamp and not a halt at a named place (the place is s2).

st.crosswalk: 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection (st.intersection); marked attribute'. A marked crosswalk is one with the marked attribute set; an unmarked crosswalk is by this contract already the prolongation at an intersection, so "at an intersection" adds nothing the contract does not state and the two alternatives together read every crosswalk the atom denotes; 'Not a stand-in for: a crosswalk' (st.sidewalk) does not apply. "at" the crosswalk: drv.position.near_region of b and the crosswalk w with the crosswalk reach, which reads st.region_geometry ('the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)'): a vehicle halted for a crossing stands before it, so occupancy (rel.occupies) would miss it. w is one crosswalk, bound once; s3 reads the same w.

Why b is stopped is a purpose, not observable (ontology §9): it is read through the conduct it explains, a pedestrian at the same crosswalk w at the same moment b is at rest at w. "a pedestrian": the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'), claimed whole. At w: drv.position.near_region of the pedestrian and w with the crosswalk reach (on the crossing included, distance zero). "to cross the roadway": a crosswalk is the portion of a highway for pedestrian crossing (DEF-NRS-484A-065), so the pedestrian at it is the one crossing; the roadway is not read separately.

"the driver of any other vehicle": ego, a vehicle (admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), not b; "the driver" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading). "approaching from the rear": drv.position.behind of ego relative to b (headings aligned, b wholly ahead of ego along ego's heading) at the beginning of the pass; it is not a stand-in for following in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane), since the passing vehicle usually travels in the adjacent lane.

"overtake and pass": drv.interaction.overtakes, ego going from wholly behind b to wholly ahead of it with aligned headings, recognized at the observation at which ego becomes wholly ahead; it is not a lane change and not contact. "such stopped vehicle": the same b that s1-s3 bind, at rest at w with a pedestrian at w.

applicability: Ego is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; driven: agency reading). The duty is engaged with respect to another vehicle b (not ego) and a crosswalk w where, at one and the same observation, b is at rest (drv.motion.at_rest, p.rest_speed_tolerance), b is at w (drv.position.near_region, p.crosswalk_reach) and some pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) is at w (drv.position.near_region, p.crosswalk_reach): at that observation where ego is behind b (drv.position.behind, p.same_direction_tolerance), and at the observation at which an overtaking of b by ego is recognized where that conjunction held at some observation while the overtaking was under way (from its onset to its recognition).
obligation: Ego does not overtake and pass such a b: drv.interaction.overtakes(ego, b) with p.same_direction_tolerance is not recognized where, at some one observation while that overtaking was under way (from the last observation at which ego was behind b to the recognition), b was at rest at a crosswalk w with a pedestrian at w. Violated at the recognition of such an overtaking; compliant otherwise.

narrowings.why: The purpose 'to permit a pedestrian to cross the roadway' is read through the conduct it explains: a pedestrian at the crosswalk b is at rest at, at the same moment; a halt at a crossing with a pedestrian at it is taken as a halt for that pedestrian.
'the driver' is read through ego's controlled motion: a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven, whoever or whatever controls it.

Ego, a motor vehicle in the left lane with aligned heading, is wholly behind b, moves alongside it and becomes wholly ahead of b while b is still at rest and the pedestrian still on w.

scenarios.narrative: Same scene; ego comes to rest in the left lane wholly behind b and stays behind until the pedestrian has left w and b has moved off; ego never becomes wholly ahead of b while b is at rest at w with a pedestrian there.

scenarios.name: blind

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but w is an unmarked crosswalk (marked attribute false), the prolongation of the sidewalks at an intersection.

scenarios.name: occasion_s1
scenarios.narrative: b rolls slowly toward w with a pedestrian on w and comes to rest within the crosswalk reach of w only once ego is already alongside it; ego then becomes wholly ahead of b.

scenarios.narrative: b was at rest at w with a pedestrian at w before ego's pass began; b starts to move before ego comes alongside, so that throughout the pass b is moving, still within the crosswalk reach of w, with the pedestrian still at w.

scenarios.name: occasion_s2
scenarios.narrative: b, at rest short of w beyond the crosswalk reach while a pedestrian is at w, creeps forward and comes to rest again within the reach of w while ego is alongside; ego becomes wholly ahead of b.

scenarios.name: occasion_s2_outside
scenarios.narrative: b was at rest within the reach of w with a pedestrian at w before ego's pass began, then crossed w and came to rest again far from any crosswalk, where ego, behind it, passes it; during the pass b is at no crosswalk.

scenarios.narrative: b is at rest at w with no pedestrian near; a pedestrian steps from the sidewalk onto w only once ego is alongside b; ego becomes wholly ahead of b.
