onset.justification: The pass's observed beginning is the last observation at which ego is behind b with aligned headings (drv.position.behind), as the concept's contract states.

occasion.recognition: the observation at which ego becomes wholly ahead of b

under_way.justification: From the onset to the recognition ego is side by side with b, the footprints' projections on ego's heading sharing a length (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero), and ego moves (kin.speed above p.rest_speed_tolerance); before the onset ego is wholly behind b. An observation inside the pass is told from one before it by ego's motion relative to b, never by a region.

param_proposals.name: p.rest_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Stop-detection noise floor: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement, set at the resolution of the speed measurement so that a complete cessation from movement is recognized despite sensor jitter.
param_proposals.source: Naturalistic-driving and simulator stop-detection practice (SHRP 2 event coding; CARLA ground-truth velocity resolution).

param_proposals.name: p.crosswalk_reach
param_proposals.convention: Reach within which a road user counts as at a crossing: a vehicle halted for a crosswalk stands within the stop-line set-back before it plus a positioning margin; a pedestrian waiting at the kerb stands within the same reach.
param_proposals.source: MUTCD (2009) Section 3B.16, stop and yield line placement before a crosswalk.

param_proposals.name: p.same_direction_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Cosine of the largest angle between two headings counted as the same direction of travel (thirty degrees), covering lane curvature and lane changes.
param_proposals.source: Trajectory-processing conventions for same-direction classification (NGSIM, highD).

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
within an intersection
intending to turn to the left
shall yield
the right-of-way
to any vehicle approaching from the opposite direction
which is within the intersection
or so close thereto as to constitute an immediate hazard,
but such driver,
having so yielded
and having given a signal when and as required,
may make such left turn
and the drivers of all other vehicles approaching the intersection from the opposite direction
shall yield
the right-of-way
to the vehicle making the left turn.

elements.justification: "a vehicle": the left-turning road user t, other than ego, of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway"); "The driver" read through its controlled motion.

"within an intersection": t's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) the intersection i (st.intersection); i is the region t's intention is declared at and the one it entered from its approach carrier c_t.

"having given a signal": t showed a left signal, its turn indicator state left (sig.turn_indicator, 'the turn indicator state ... left') or an arm signal of meaning left (sig.hand_signal), at some observation since its latest stretch on its approach carrier c_t into i began; the signal itself, not a declared intention, and not the turn. "when and as required": the timing and manner another statute sets, outside this corpus; the signal is read as given at or before the judged observation.

"may make such left turn": t is making the left turn it intends, drv.motion.turning_left (moving with its heading turning to the left at or above the yaw tolerance), a turn under way rather than one completed. The turn under way is one continuous stretch: drv.motion.turning_left has held for t at every observation since the observation at which it last rose (the turn's observed onset), and that onset is the moment at which "having so yielded" (f10) is read.

"the drivers of all other vehicles": ego, a vehicle (admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) other than t, its driver read through its controlled motion. "approaching the intersection": ego occupies (rel.occupies) a carrier c_e (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters), the ontology's reading of a road user's approach to an intersection, whatever its motion. "from the opposite direction": c_e and the carrier c_t from which t entered i carry opposed designated directions (st.lane_direction), as rel.oncoming's contract directs, not the current headings, which t's turn changes.
"shall yield": granting precedence (DEF-NRS-484A-210 "unless one grants precedence to the other"): ego is at rest (drv.motion.at_rest) or not in conflict with t (operationalization of f15).
"the vehicle making the left turn": the same t, turning left (drv.motion.turning_left) at the judged observation, within the continuous turning stretch of f12.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: DEF-NRS-484A-210 "approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other"
operationalizations.convention: Traffic-conflict technique: two road users are in conflict where, projected at their current velocities, their centres approach within the time-to-collision horizon and their closest-approach centre distance is below the clearance at which their bodies would touch. Direction, speed and proximity enter by degree through the projected velocities and positions.

intentions.meaning: The road user's current plan includes turning left at the target region.

applicability: Ego is a vehicle (driven: agency reading) occupying a carrier c_e (st.travel_region, rel.occupies) whose entrance end is an intersection i (st.lane_enters), and some vehicle t other than ego (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) at the judged observation: overlaps i (rel.occupies); declares int.left_turn at i; is turning left (drv.motion.turning_left, p.turn_yaw_tolerance, p.rest_speed_tolerance) and has been turning left at every observation since the observation at which drv.motion.turning_left last rose for it (the onset of the turn under way); has, at that onset, "so yielded": there is an earlier or equal observation at which t occupied a carrier c_t (st.travel_region, rel.occupies) whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters) while not overlapping i, and at every observation after it up to and including the onset t overlapped i and complied with NRS_484B_253_o1 (t as its ego) — compliance read only up to the onset, since "having so yielded" is past to the turn, and NOT at the observations of the turn after it; showed a left signal (sig.turn_indicator left or sig.hand_signal left) at some observation since its latest stretch on c_t began (no rise of its occupancy of c_t after the signal); and c_t's and c_e's designated directions (st.lane_direction) have a dot product below minus p.opposite_direction_tolerance.
obligation: Ego is at rest (drv.motion.at_rest, p.rest_speed_tolerance), or for every intersection i, carrier c_e and vehicle t selected exactly as in the applicability (the whole selection re-bound: ego on c_e entering i; t other than ego, a vehicle, overlapping i, declaring int.left_turn at i, turning left continuously since the turn's onset, having entered i from an opposed carrier c_t and complied with NRS_484B_253_o1 from that entry up to and including the onset, and having signalled left since its latest stretch on c_t began), ego is not in conflict with t: not both prim.closest_approach_within(ego, t) with horizon p.conflict_horizon and prim.closest_approach_distance(ego, t) with the same horizon below p.conflict_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'the drivers' are read through the vehicles' controlled motion.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Vehicle t entered the intersection from its approach lane with int.left_turn and its left indicator on since its approach, waited at rest while ego, approaching from the opposite direction, was far off, and began its left turn at an observation at which its projected closest approach with ego did not lie within p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_clearance (so t complied with NRS_484B_253_o1 up to its onset). t turns slowly; ego keeps moving without slowing, and at a later observation of the same turn their projected closest approach lies within p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene as forbid; ego slows and comes to rest at the edge of the intersection, and is at rest at every observation at which its projected closest approach with the turning t would lie within p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_clearance, until t completes its turn.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: t crosses the intersection straight ahead (int.left_turn false, not turning left); ego approaches from the opposite direction.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Scene of forbid, but the source declares sig.turn_indicator and sig.hand_signal absent: whether t signalled cannot be read.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but t's indicator stayed off and it gave no arm signal: t gave no signal, so the opposing drivers' duty does not arise.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but t began its turn at an observation at which ego, approaching from the opposite direction, was within the immediate-hazard distance of the intersection and their projected closest approach lay within p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_clearance: t did not yield as NRS_484B_253_o1 requires up to its onset, so the duty to yield to it does not arise.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but t's indicator stays off and it gives a left arm signal (sig.hand_signal left) since its approach: the signal is given, and ego, in conflict with the turning t, has not yielded.

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: Ego approaches the intersection alone on its approach lane; no other road user is in the scene.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
approaching an intersection
shall yield
the right-of-way
to a vehicle which has entered the intersection from a different highway.
Except as otherwise provided in subsection 4 [NRS-484B-250-4],
this section does not apply at intersections controlled by official traffic-control devices
or to vehicles approaching each other from opposite directions,
when the driver of one of the vehicles is intending to
or is making a left turn.

elements.justification: "a vehicle": the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; "The driver" read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading).

"approaching an intersection": ego occupies (rel.occupies) a carrier c whose entrance end is the intersection i (st.lane_enters: 'a road user occupying one such carrier approaches through it whatever its motion') and does not overlap i, or enters i at the judged observation from such a c. Not inferred from heading or distance.

"yield": granting precedence (DEF-NRS-484A-210 "unless one grants precedence to the other"): ego does not proceed while the vehicle with the right-of-way is in conflict with it, so ego is at rest (drv.motion.at_rest) or not in conflict (operationalization of e4).

"a vehicle": a road user b other than ego of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. "has entered the intersection": b's footprint overlaps i (rel.occupies) after an entry from a carrier c_b whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters), read through a past operator. "from a different highway": c_b lies (st.on_way) on a highway (st.highway) on which ego's carrier c does not lie; the intersection itself lies on every way that meets there and is no evidence of either.

"official traffic-control devices" (DEF-NRS-484A-145 'every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority or railroad for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic'), qualified by the law's own word "controlled": the devices that control an intersection, a traffic signal head (dev.traffic_signal), a stop sign (dev.stop_sign) or a yield sign (dev.yield_sign), governing (dev.governs) the intersection i or any carrier whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters), whichever entrance it governs. The word leaves out devices that only warn or guide (speed-limit and zone signs, warning signs, markings) and devices of other kinds. "official": status read through the device's presence.

"vehicles approaching each other from opposite directions": ego and b, vehicles (admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), whose approach carriers into i (ego's carrier c, and the carrier c_b from which b entered; st.lane_enters) carry opposed designated directions (st.lane_direction), read through the carriers as rel.oncoming's contract directs, never through current headings, which a turn changes.

"or is making a left turn": ego or b is turning left (drv.motion.turning_left: moving, its heading turning to the left at or above the yaw tolerance), a turn under way at the judged observation, at the intersection i the words concern.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: DEF-NRS-484A-210 "approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other"
operationalizations.convention: Traffic-conflict technique: two road users are in conflict where, projected at their current velocities, their centres approach within the time-to-collision horizon and their closest-approach centre distance is below the clearance at which their bodies would touch. Direction, speed and proximity enter by degree through the projected velocities and positions.

intentions.meaning: The road user's current plan includes turning left at the target region.

applicability: Ego is a vehicle (driven: agency reading) approaching an intersection i (on a carrier c whose entrance end is i, not overlapping i, or entering i from c at the judged observation); and no traffic signal, stop sign or yield sign governs i or any carrier entering i (dev.traffic_signal, dev.stop_sign, dev.yield_sign, dev.governs, st.lane_enters), this exception being suspended where NRS_484B_250_4_o1 or NRS_484B_250_4_o2 applies to ego.
obligation: For every vehicle b other than ego whose footprint overlaps i after an entry from a carrier c_b lying on a highway on which c does not lie (st.on_way): not where c and c_b carry opposed directions (st.lane_direction, the dot product of the two directions below minus p.opposite_direction_tolerance) and ego or b declares int.left_turn at i or is turning left (drv.motion.turning_left with p.turn_yaw_tolerance and p.rest_speed_tolerance); otherwise ego is at rest (drv.motion.at_rest, p.rest_speed_tolerance) or not in conflict with b: not both prim.closest_approach_within(ego, b) with horizon p.conflict_horizon and prim.closest_approach_distance(ego, b) with the same horizon below p.conflict_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'The driver' is read through ego's controlled motion.
'official' is read through the presence of the device governing the intersection or an approach to it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: No device governs the intersection or its approaches. Ego approaches on highway A; vehicle b has entered from highway B and is crossing; ego keeps moving and enters while their projected closest approach lies within p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene; ego slows and comes to rest at the edge of the intersection until b has cleared, then enters with no projected conflict.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: Stop signs govern the approaches of highway B: the intersection is controlled by official traffic-control devices, and no inoperative signal is involved.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Scene of forbid, but the source declares st.lane_enters absent: whether ego approaches the intersection cannot be read.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: No device governs the intersection. Vehicle b entered from the opposite approach of ego's own highway A; no vehicle from a different highway is within the intersection; ego enters.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: An inoperative traffic signal governs the intersection (NRS_484B_250_4_o1 applies to ego's entry), so the device exception is suspended; ego enters in conflict with b, which entered from highway B.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: No device governs the intersection and ego approaches and enters with no other road user in the scene.

param_proposals.name: p.rest_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Stop-detection noise floor: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement, set at the resolution of the speed measurement so that a complete cessation from movement is recognized despite sensor jitter.
param_proposals.source: Naturalistic-driving and simulator stop-detection practice (SHRP 2 event coding; CARLA ground-truth velocity resolution).

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: Time-to-collision horizon of the traffic-conflict technique: a projected approach of the centres within this time counts toward the danger of a crash.
param_proposals.source: Hayward (1972) time-to-collision; Hyden (1987) Swedish Traffic Conflict Technique; van der Horst (1990) TTC thresholds.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_clearance
param_proposals.convention: Centre-to-centre distance at the projected closest approach below which the bodies of two passenger vehicles would touch or nearly touch (about a half-length plus a half-width of a design passenger car).
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book, design vehicle P dimensions.

param_proposals.name: p.opposite_direction_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Cosine of the largest angle off exactly opposed at which two approach directions still count as opposite (thirty degrees), covering skewed approaches.
param_proposals.source: Trajectory-processing conventions for opposing-movement classification at intersections (inD).

param_proposals.name: p.turn_yaw_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Yaw rate below which a change of heading counts as none: above lane-keeping yaw noise, below the yaw rates of turning at a junction.
param_proposals.source: Vehicle-dynamics practice for turn-onset detection from yaw-rate sensors.
